Cobicistat increases the levels of berotralstat through interactions with other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Berotralstat can elevate the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of P-gp substrates if coadministered. 4. Atazanavir enhances the effects of betaxolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, atrioventricular (AV) block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider reducing the beta-blocker dose and monitor closely. 5. Atazanavir and betibeglogene autotemcel interaction requires avoiding or using alternative drugs. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before mobilization or during apheresis cycles, as they may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 6. Cobicistat increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor closely. 7. Atazanavir elevates bexarotene levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir enhances bisoprolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Bosentan decreases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Bosentan dose reduction is necessary. 11.
